dedupe_keys.name: united nations register and online index of objects launched into outer space

description: The United Nations Register of Objects Launched into Outer Space is the official international register of satellites, probes and other objects placed in orbit or beyond, kept by the UN Office for Outer Space Affairs since 1962 under General Assembly resolution 1721B and, since 1976, the Registration Convention. States and international organisations that are party to the Convention must keep national registries and send the Secretary-General information on each object, such as its designator, launch date and site, basic orbital parameters (period, inclination, apogee and perigee) and general function, and later changes of status such as decay or transfer of ownership. The Online Index of Objects Launched into Outer Space makes this searchable, listing more than 17,000 objects with their names, launching states, status and launch dates, and offers exports as a ZIP file with a CSV table, JSON metadata and a readme; UNOOSA also publishes the official submissions as UN documents and guidance on registration practice. Coverage: worldwide, 1957 to present. Format and access: online index with CSV export and UN documents, free. Caveats: registration is often late or incomplete, especially for large constellations, and the index was temporarily unavailable during an IT change reported in search results. Simulation uses: ownership and jurisdiction of satellites for governance scenarios, national dependence on space assets and cross-checking orbital catalogues. Related records: CelesTrak, ESA DISCOS and the ITU Space Network List cover orbital elements, physical properties and frequency filings.
